query: Add a mode that overlaps two molecules on a per-atom scalar field the Molecule doesn't carry yet, scored as an INDEPENDENT Gaussian field channel rather than a shape-weighted one, then blended with shape.
expected_behavior: Recognizes that get_overlap_esp folds the shape Gaussian into its field overlap and is therefore NOT usable for an independent field -- the whole vol_lipo / vol_mr / vol_fukui family is shape-weighted by construction -- so it writes a new pure overlap in score/<family>_scoring.py, inputs in and scalar out, no optimization.

Decides the _np / _jax mirror question deliberately and says which way it went, citing the precedent both ways: gaussian_overlap / electrostatic_scoring / pharmacophore_scoring keep mirrors, while score/atomtype_scoring.py is intentionally torch-only. Does not edit a mirror halfway.
Verifies by hand that the new channel scores exactly 1.000 for a molecule against itself under Tanimoto, matching numerator and self-overlap widths and masks.

Adds the per-atom property to Molecule via the four-part accessor pattern, as a full (N,) RDKit-mol-order array sliced by the same _nonH_atoms_idx the charges use, including the get_<feature>_positions() centres accessor so MoleculeProfile can duck-type the same name later; chooses eager storage for a cheap descriptor or a lazy property for an expensive one and says why.
Guards both per-atom traps -- atom order and the retained-H basis -- and keeps gate 5; keeps the planted-pose gate, which is the only gate that catches a consistently-wrong atom-order mapping.

Names objective_/optimize_ by mode id; registers only _ALIGN_KEYS; align_with_<mode> uses literal defaults; exports the alignment functions from alignment/__init__.py and nothing from the empty score/__init__.py.

Hands off to accelerate-scoring-mode stating the optimizer name, the test path, the gradient structure, AND the fact that new per-atom Molecule data was added -- the last because both the batched path and the screening store must learn to carry that array.
